transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Well, I came in because... I just keep hearing these voices. It's clear as a bell, like somebody is standing right there in my little studio with me. They keep saying my name and telling me my work is being judged. 

Which just isn't fair, because I work really hard. I'm a personal care aide, and my main lady, Mrs. Higgins, she's a handful. I have to take the bus all the way down 4th street to get to her, and the bus driver always brakes so hard. The other day I almost spilled my coffee right on this man's shoes. He was wearing those expensive leather loafers, too, the kind my uncle used to wear to church. Uncle Earl always said you can tell a lot about a man by his shoes, you know? He used to polish his every Saturday night while listening to the radio. 

But anyway, even when I get back home from work and the house is completely quiet... nobody is there... I still hear them talking to me, saying my name and telling me I'm being judged.
How long have you been hearing these voices?

Well, let me think... it's been about nine months now. Nine months of the voices, and just this... this constant, fixed fear that my work is being watched all the time. 

It started right around the time it got really cold last year. I remember because my little space heater just sparked and died, and I had to walk all the way down to that hardware store on Elm Street to get a new one. You know the one? It has that faded orange awning out front. The owner, Mr. Gable, he keeps this massive fluffy cat right on the checkout counter. A Maine Coon, I think they're called. They have those little tufts of hair on their ears. I'd love to have a cat to keep me company in the studio, but I can't. Mrs. Higgins is terribly allergic, and if I got cat dander on my scrubs, oh, she would just have an absolute fit. She already complains about my laundry detergent being too floral, even though it's just the cheap kind from the dollar store. You really can't beat their prices on cleaning supplies, though.
Since the voices began, have you had a period lasting at least two weeks when you felt depressed nearly every day or lost interest in most things?

Depressed? No, I don't think so. I haven't really felt sad or stopped doing my usual things. I mean, I still have to keep busy, you know? Like with my shows. I watch that game show with the big spinning wheel every morning before I catch the bus to Mrs. Higgins' place. I swear, I always guess the puzzle way before the people on the television do. 

My neighbor, Betty, she came over once to borrow some sugar while it was on, and she just couldn't believe how fast I was getting the words. Betty makes this incredible meatloaf, by the way. She puts just a little pinch of brown sugar right into the ketchup glaze on top. It sounds a little strange, I know, but it just caramelizes so beautifully when you bake it. I tried to make it myself last Tuesday, but my oven runs so hot, and I ended up scorching the bottom of my good glass dish. I was scrubbing that pan for what felt like hours, using that dollar store soap I told you about. You really have to let it soak first if you burn sugar onto glass, otherwise you'll just ruin your sponges. 

But um... what was I saying? Oh, right. No, I haven't been down in the dumps or anything like that. Just... just dealing with those voices telling me I'm being judged.
Have you used any recreational drugs, misused prescription medicines, or unusually increased your alcohol use since the voices began?

No, I haven't been taking any drugs or drinking more or anything like that. I've never really been one for drinking, to be honest. My ex-husband, now he could put away a twelve-pack on a Saturday without even blinking. He used to leave those empty cans all over the coffee table, the one with the little water rings on it that I could never get out. I tried coasters, you know, those nice cork ones with the little roosters painted on them? I got them at a yard sale down the street from this lovely older couple. They were moving to Florida to be closer to their grandchildren. Florida seems so hot, though. I don't know how people deal with all that humidity. My hair gets so frizzy just when it rains here. I have to use this special smoothing serum, but it smells a little bit like coconuts, which I'm not crazy about. But anyway, no, no drugs or anything like that for me.
Since the voices and fear of being judged began, have you had trouble doing your job?

Well, yes, actually. It's been really hard with Mrs. Higgins and the other clients. I started missing shifts, and I was getting all my care notes mixed up. I just couldn't keep my visits organized like I used to. It's terrible because I've always been so organized. I used to have this wonderful little planner, a blue one with gold lettering on the front. I bought it at that little stationery shop downtown, the one next to the bakery that makes those amazing lemon tarts. Have you ever had one? They put just a little bit of powdered sugar on top, and the crust is so flaky it just melts in your mouth. I tried to bake lemon tarts once for my walking club—oh, I stopped going to that, too, and my library art talks. I just stay home alone mostly now. But anyway, the tarts were a disaster. The lemon filling didn't set right, and it was just this yellow puddle in the middle of the crust. I think I didn't use enough cornstarch. You really have to measure cornstarch perfectly, or it just ruins the whole consistency of whatever you're making. My grandmother used to say baking is a science, but cooking is an art. She was such a good cook. But yes, my job... it got to the point where I was really in danger of losing it because of all the mix-ups.
Do you hear the voices even when you are not thinking about being watched or judged?

Well, I guess... yes, I do. The voices are just there, even when I'm just sitting by myself, not worrying about anyone looking at me. Like yesterday, I was just trying to sort my laundry. I have this system where I separate the darks, the lights, and then the delicates. You really have to be careful with delicates. I ruined a perfectly good silk blouse once because I accidentally tossed it in with the heavy towels. It was this beautiful emerald green color, the kind that really brings out your eyes if you have hazel eyes like my sister does. She always wore green, even to her wedding, which was a little unconventional, but it suited her. Her husband, Tom, he wore a gray suit with a little green pocket square to match. They had the reception at this lovely old barn they converted into an event space. The catering was fantastic, they had these little bacon-wrapped scallops that were just to die for. I must have eaten five of them before the main course even came out. But anyway, yes, the voices... they just talk to me even when I'm not thinking about the judgment thing.
